**Course source:** Day 4 §3. **Running example:** a shop with Product, Order and User services.

## A configuration platform with managed releases

The course finishes with **Apollo**, an open-source configuration-management system, and covers its architecture, server deployment and client integration.

Unlike a simple shared file, a dedicated configuration platform can offer administrative controls, application namespaces, environment separation, release history and client update mechanisms. These features are operational capabilities; they do not remove the need for validation and safe rollout.

## Apply it to the shop

Order could read a non-secret deadline property from an environment-specific namespace:

~~~text
application: order
environment: STG
namespace:   checkout
key:         product.timeout.ms
value:       350
~~~

The representation above is conceptual. A real Apollo deployment has its own published APIs and configuration model.

## Publication workflow

A developer proposes changing the timeout; a reviewer approves it; the platform publishes a new configuration version; instances receive or fetch updates; the release is monitored and possibly rolled back.

This process should answer: **who changed what, where, when and why?** That audit history is especially important when one bad configuration can affect all replicas.

## Failure and security design

Protect administrative APIs, distinguish read and write permissions, secure client transport and decide what settings may be cached locally when Apollo is unavailable. Do not put credentials in public documentation.

## Compare with Spring Cloud Config

Both address distributed configuration, but their administration models, integration assumptions and change workflows differ. Choose based on operational needs—controlled release, multi-environment governance, failure behaviour and supported client stacks—not because one appears later in a historical course.

[Official Apollo project](https://github.com/apolloconfig/apollo).

## Questions to answer aloud

What problem does this design solve? Which guarantee does it give, and which guarantee does it **not** give? How would you detect incorrect operation?

## Mathematical Abstraction

Configuration publication is a versioned transition.

$$
C^{(v)}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{approved\ release}}C^{(v+1)}
$$

This is a governance model: approval, distribution and effective application are distinct events, not an atomic global transaction.
